claim_scope: A maker-published real PC design combining a visible digital desktop and keyboard with an exposed mechanism-like tier and historical cabinet/instrument forms. A scoped Steampunk formal comparator, not evidence that the visible gears perform computation or use steam.
limits: The general workshop story does not authenticate the composition, antiquity, mechanism, drive system or material of each part in this item. Exact maker, dates, full specifications and working operation remain unverified. Small lamps, telephone and framed portrait remain around the PC but do not obscure its screen, keyboard or mechanism tier; these are not necessary style props. The portrait is not evidence of the device’s age.
observable_features: A complete upright monitor and lower round-key keyboard form a single central cabinet-like computer assembly in a front three-quarter view.
A digital desktop with small icons and a taskbar is visible within the decorated rectangular screen surround.
Between screen and keyboard, rows of exposed toothed wheels, rods and cylindrical forms create a contrasting mechanical-looking tier.
A curved broken-pediment-like top, dark wood-grain fields and metallic-looking borders integrate historical furniture/instrument vocabulary with the modern interface.
The neutral wall, unreflected screen and close framing remove the old photo’s star-pattern tablecloth and competing dark wall field.

association_evidence.supports: The workshop’s actual About gallery exposes this exact image and identifies it in alt/title/data-title as The Clacker PC 2. The general story describes modern computer equipment reworked through historical design languages; it does not date this item, name its individual maker or prove every part’s material or function.

confusion_check.shared_appearances: Dark cabinetry, metallic trim, round keys and old instruments can also occur in genuine antiques or simple vintage decoration.
confusion_check.discriminating_relationships: A directly visible modern digital interface and computer-keyboard arrangement occupy the same cabinet as exposed wheel/shaft forms and historical furniture contours. Their integrated modern-device/historical-machine relation is stronger than an isolated brass color or a decorative gear sticker. Do not claim that the visible mechanism powers the PC.
confusion_check.cannot_conclude: The image cannot establish steam power, a working mechanical computer, authentic antique components, precise metallurgy, item dates or all Steampunk media.
